feedback.answered: The second obligation is settled in scope. Direct check a7ab7f88 executed its fixed bytes (execution 1987811182294bfbb372a36548be8d8b) with prerequisites matched, comparison_complete and witness_complete true, and outcome violated: one declared out-of-window pure heartbeat was rejected with ErrUnsupportedProtocol and changed nothing on the normal path (processRPC -> checkRPCHeader), while the heartbeat fast path (processHeartbeat -> appendEntries) advanced the persisted term from 0 to 5, adopted the sender as known leader, refreshed last contact and reported guard_applied false. The in-window control was accepted on the normal path, so the difference is attributable to the RPC-header window rather than the request shape. The blocking review issue was the threading conflict between processHeartbeat's comment and the transport's concurrent invocation; it was resolved as an independent scope boundary rather than by weakening the claim.
remaining: Whether an out-of-window peer can deliver a pure heartbeat in a legal deployment, and whether the absent guard is deliberate design (in which case the correct disposition is a documented assumption), are the residual premises of claim-heartbeat-header-gate.
The election consequence of refreshing last contact on the fast path was not measured; a check would need a running node plus a heartbeat source.

The concurrency question itself (whether processHeartbeat may be invoked off the main thread at all, given its comment and the lock-protected fields it touches) remains an independent limit with no obligation yet.
